Method of Attack: Ransomware infection built using a builder that allows creation of customized ransomware variants
Encrypts files with customizable encrypted file extensions
Uses TEA or XOR encryption algorithms
Victims instructed to send SMS with special ID to designated number to receive decryption password
Uses a standard ransom note message by default
Targets a wide range of file extensions for encryption
Password prompt for decryption with limited attempts
Files added include %Temp%\[random].exe and %UserProfile%\Desktop\HOW TO DECRYPT FILES.txt
Impacted Systems: Windows systems (implied by file paths and ransomware behavior)

Files with extensions: zip, rar, 7z, tar, gzip, jpg, jpeg, psd, cdr, dwg, max, bmp, gif, png, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx, txt, pdf, djvu, htm, html, mdb, cer, p12, pfx, kwm, pwm, 1cd, md, mdf, dbf, odt, vob, ifo, lnk, torrent, mov, m2v, 3gp, mpeg, mpg, flv, avi, mp4, wmv, divx, mkv, mp3, wav, flac, ape, wma, ac3
Attack Vector: Distribution of customized ransomware executable created by the builder
Likely distributed by malware distributors purchasing the builder from darkweb malware and exploit forums
Indicators of Compromise: Ransom note file named HOW TO DECRYPT FILES.txt
